subject: business-studies
title: Ethics Stretch Adventure
welcome_lead: Exam-style stretch. Evaluate whether ethical strategies hurt or help profits — using stakeholder analysis.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies stretch — evaluating ethics vs profit and stakeholder impact analysis.
final_note: You can evaluate ethical strategies on profit and use stakeholders to structure analysis.

concepts.def: Pretending to be eco-friendly without real action
Trying to make as much profit as possible
How a business is viewed by the public
Pay enough to meet basic living costs
Group lobbying firms to change behaviour

walkthroughs.body_html:
Ethical action may raise short-term cost but build long-term value through reputation and loyalty.

Cheap unethical shortcuts can backfire badly when uncovered.

Shareholders may want max dividends. Customers want fair pricing. Staff want fair pay.

Managers must balance these or face strikes, boycotts, or sell-offs.

Greenwashing = pretending to be eco-friendly to win sales without changing.

Modern consumers and pressure groups expose it fast — and the brand damage is severe.

options: Genuine environmental action
Marketing exaggerating eco-credentials
Recycling targets
Cleaning factories

mcqs.q: Paying the LIVING WAGE may lead to.
options: Lower staff motivation
Higher labour costs but better retention
No effect at all
Reduced customer trust

mcqs.q: What is the difference between profit and revenue?
options: Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
Profit and revenue are different words for the same thing.
Revenue is total income from sales (price x quantity sold); profit is revenue minus total costs — what is left after paying for everything.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a stakeholder and a shareholder?
options: Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
Stakeholders are managers and shareholders are workers.
Stakeholders and shareholders are different spellings of the same word.
A shareholder owns shares in the company; a stakeholder is anyone affected by or with interest in the business — employees, customers, suppliers, community, plus shareholders.

mcqs.q: Why can a profitable business still fail?
options: If a business is profitable it cannot run out of money.
Stakeholders are managers and shareholders are workers.
Because cash flow and profit are different — a business may be profitable on paper but run out of cash to pay bills, especially if customers owe money or stock ties up funds.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
